t: The Time When the Network Becomes Idle - One BFS Plus Timing Arithmetic
o: Every data server pings the master (node 0) at second 0; a message d hops away needs d seconds to arrive and its reply another d seconds to return, so a message sent at time t keeps channels busy until t + 2d. While waiting, server i repeats its message every patience[i] seconds and stops forever once any reply arrives. The network is idle only when the very last in-flight reply has landed. In example 1 server 2 sits d = 2 away with patience 1: it resends at seconds 1, 2, 3; the reply to the third resend lands at second 7, and from the beginning of second 8 nothing moves - that is the answer. With n up to 10^5 we need one distance computation shared by all servers, not one per server.
k: A single BFS from the master yields every server distance d; each message round trip takes 2d seconds.
A server's last send happens at floor((2d - 1) / patience) * patience - the latest multiple of its period strictly before the first reply returns at 2d.
The network idles one second after the last final-send reply lands: answer = max(lastSend + 2d) + 1.

a.n: Approach 1: BFS from Every Data Server
a.i: Give each data server its own BFS to find its distance to node 0, then apply the timing arithmetic. Running a full BFS per server costs O(n * (n + m)) overall - wasteful, but it cleanly separates graph traversal from the simulation logic.
s: Build the adjacency list from the undirected edges.
For each data server, BFS to find its hop distance d to node 0.
Set rt = 2d and the last resend at (rt - 1) / patience * patience using integer division.
Return the maximum of last + rt over all data servers, plus one.
a.t: O(n * (n + m)) - one complete BFS per data server; degrades badly near n = 10^5.
a.sp: O(n + m) - adjacency list, queue, and distance array reused per BFS.

a.i: One BFS rooted at the master supplies every distance. Data server i sees its first reply at the beginning of second 2d_i, so it resends at the multiples of patience[i] strictly below that instant; the latest such send is last = floor((2d - 1) / p) * p, which correctly yields 0 whenever 2d <= p. That final message's reply lands at last + 2d, and the earliest fully idle second is one past the maximum landing time.
s: BFS from node 0 once to fill dist[].
For each i >= 1 compute rt = 2 * dist[i] and last = (rt - 1) / patience[i] * patience[i].
Track the maximum of last + rt across all data servers.
a.t: O(n + m) - a single BFS plus one arithmetic pass over the servers.
a.sp: O(n + m) - adjacency list, distance array, and queue.

w: Two details sink most attempts: the trailing +1 (a reply arriving at the beginning of second T still occupies second T, so idleness starts at T + 1), and the strict "before 2d" cutoff for the final resend - using floor(2d / p) * p would resend at the exact moment the first reply arrives. Sanity-check the formula on 2d <= patience (never resends, idle at 2d + 1) before coding. Follow-ups: asymmetric travel times (Dijkstra instead of BFS), or a master processing delay L added to every reply.
